presentation.summary: Manage a hot-work job beside operating hydrocarbon equipment while conditions change and a fire emergency develops.
presentation.role: You are the site safety professional coordinating a hot-work task in an operating hydrocarbon area.
presentation.situation: A welding crew is ready to work beside live process equipment. The job depends on permit integrity, isolation, gas testing, fire prevention, SIMOPS control and disciplined emergency response.
presentation.objective: Keep ignition and fuel hazards controlled from authorization through closeout, and intervene early when conditions change.
knownFacts: A hot-work permit has been prepared.
Flammable atmosphere and hidden combustible materials remain credible hazards.
Nearby operations can change conditions during the job.

hot_work_permit.title: Hot-work permit
hot_work_permit.summary: Hot-work permit defines the authorized scope, conditions, hold points and required controls for the work.
hot_work_permit.details:
Check that the scope and location match the actual task.
Confirm required controls and hold points are satisfied.
Treat changed conditions as a trigger for reassessment.

gas_test_record.title: Atmospheric test record
gas_test_record.summary: Atmospheric test record shows atmospheric results, test timing and the basis for continued monitoring.
gas_test_record.details:
Confirm the document applies to this job and equipment.
Check current status, limits and any unresolved conditions.
Use it together with field verification rather than as a substitute for field conditions.

isolation_record.title: Isolation record
isolation_record.summary: Isolation record identifies hazardous-energy or process-isolation controls and how their effectiveness is verified.
isolation_record.details:

fire_watch_plan.summary: Fire-watch plan provides task-specific information needed to verify controls before work proceeds.

authorization_decision_defensible.observable: The action improves control at the authorize the hot-work task stage, but one important verification or scope gap remains. Work proceeds with less assurance.
authorization_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This is professionally plausible and partly correct, but it leaves one material criterion unresolved compared with the BEST action.

authorization_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the authorize the hot-work task stage before exposure continues. The hot-work task moves forward from a controlled condition.
authorization_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

authorization_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the authorize the hot-work task stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
authorization_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

authorization_decision_critical.observable: The hot-work task proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the authorize the hot-work task stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
authorization_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

fire_prevention_decision_defensible.observable: The action improves control at the build the fire-prevention barrier stage, but one important verification or scope gap remains. Work proceeds with less assurance.
fire_prevention_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This is professionally plausible and partly correct, but it leaves one material criterion unresolved compared with the BEST action.

fire_prevention_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the build the fire-prevention barrier stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
fire_prevention_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

fire_prevention_decision_critical.observable: The hot-work task proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the build the fire-prevention barrier stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
fire_prevention_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

fire_prevention_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the build the fire-prevention barrier stage before exposure continues. The hot-work task moves forward from a controlled condition.
fire_prevention_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

changing_conditions_decision_best.observable: The team stops or stabilizes the work when conditions change at the respond to a changing atmosphere stage. The new condition is verified before the task continues.
changing_conditions_decision_best.guidedInsight: Changing conditions invalidate earlier assumptions. The BEST response creates a deliberate hold point and reassesses the controls before exposure continues.

changing_conditions_decision_defensible.observable: The team pauses part of the activity and gathers more information, but some exposure or uncertainty remains during the respond to a changing atmosphere stage.
changing_conditions_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This choice recognizes the change, yet it leaves a narrower safety margin than a full stop-and-reassess response.

changing_conditions_decision_weak.observable: The work continues under modified monitoring or local precautions even though the respond to a changing atmosphere condition has changed materially. Risk begins to rise.
changing_conditions_decision_weak.guidedInsight: Extra observation is not equivalent to restoring a failed or uncertain barrier. Changed conditions should be controlled, not merely watched.

changing_conditions_decision_critical.observable: The changed condition is effectively accepted and the hot-work task continues. A critical barrier is lost and the scenario moves into emergency territory.
changing_conditions_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Proceeding because an alarm limit, schedule or visible condition has not yet become extreme can miss the earlier point where safe intervention was still easy.

emergency_decision_defensible.observable: The immediate area is secured and help is mobilized, but one element of the control the developing fire response remains less complete than the preferred plan.
emergency_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This action can reduce harm, but the BEST response integrates personnel protection, alarm, isolation and planned emergency control without leaving a material response gap.

emergency_decision_weak.observable: Some protective action is taken, but personnel remain closer to the hazard than necessary during the control the developing fire response. The margin for a secondary casualty narrows.
emergency_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A partial emergency action may sound practical, but it is weak when it keeps people exposed or delays full hazard-zone control.

emergency_decision_best.observable: The team activates the planned emergency response at the control the developing fire stage, keeps people out of the hazard zone and controls the event before re-entry.
emergency_decision_best.guidedInsight: The strongest emergency choice protects responders first. Rescue, isolation and source control should follow the planned capability rather than expose another person.

emergency_decision_critical.observable: An unprotected or inadequately controlled intervention is attempted during the control the developing fire stage. The event escalates and a secondary casualty or larger release becomes credible.
emergency_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Critical emergency decisions often fail by sending people toward an uncontrolled hazard. Protect responders and establish control before attempting intervention.

closeout_decision_defensible.observable: The team strengthens the immediate controls and uses a controlled restart review, but the closeout does not explore the underlying failure as completely as the BEST path.
closeout_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: Corrective action is valuable, but restart assurance is stronger when the underlying cause and all affected safeguards are verified.

closeout_decision_best.observable: The hot-work task remains suspended while causes, damaged safeguards and corrective actions are verified. Work is reauthorized only after a safe basis is re-established.
closeout_decision_best.guidedInsight: Safe closeout is not simply returning conditions to normal. It must address why control was lost and verify the barriers needed for a safe restart.

closeout_decision_weak.observable: The team corrects the most visible problem and prepares to resume the hot-work task before the full causal chain has been resolved.
closeout_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A technically acceptable local fix can still be weak if it restores production before learning and system-level corrections are complete.

closeout_decision_critical.observable: The hot-work task is pushed toward restart after only superficial recovery. Critical causes or damaged safeguards remain unresolved.
closeout_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Restart pressure can recreate the same hazard. A major event is more likely when work resumes before critical barriers are restored and verified.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The hot-work task was completed with the critical hazards controlled and changing conditions managed before escalation.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: You verified the critical controls before ignition sources were introduced and stopped when conditions changed.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: The hot-work task developed a significant control weakness, but later decisions restored a controlled state before serious harm occurred.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: A control gap emerged, but intervention restored safe control before the event could escalate.

incident_contained.title: Incident contained
incident_contained.narrative: The scenario developed into an incident, but emergency and recovery actions contained the event and limited its consequences.
incident_contained.keyTurningPoint: The fire developed, but alarm, isolation and response actions limited the consequences.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control failures allowed the hot-work task to escalate into a major incident requiring extended response, investigation and corrective action.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Warning signs were not controlled early enough, allowing fire and process hazards to combine.

critical_failure.title: Critical failure
critical_failure.narrative: The decision path produced a severe uncontrolled outcome in the hot-work task. Recovery options were overwhelmed by a critical barrier failure.
critical_failure.keyTurningPoint: A critical ignition or emergency barrier was bypassed at the decisive moment.
